title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared model gpt-5-mini, we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks drawn from three vendor-CLI families and small topology templates. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared_initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, execution accounting diagnostics, an artifact-grounded explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for intent-driven network operations (intent→configuration and intent→workflow) and AIOps co-pilot workflows. Operational trustworthiness for agentic NetOps pipelines depends not only on model output quality but crucially on surrounding validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution that can detect or mitigate incorrect or unsafe outputs [1], [2]. Prior work recommends generate→validate→repair architectures and prototype runtime emulation, but quantitative cross-vendor estimates of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation beyond a strong static validator are scarce. We therefore posed the preregistered confirmatory research question: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contribution is an artifact-grounded paired measurement using a frozen preregistration and the archived execution and analysis artifacts supporting exact, reproducible claims.
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent system reports emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—static validators, formal verification tools, and sandboxed execution—to reduce NetOps operational risk and to make LLM-driven pipelines auditable [1], [2]. Prototype tools have adapted program-verification ideas to network configuration analysis and shown cases where dynamic execution or higher-fidelity checks expose problems missed by static checks [3]. Empirical studies from adjacent domains report that external verifiers improve correctness in code and specification generation, while LLMs alone can hallucinate or fail to locate their own reasoning errors [4]. These findings motivate paired, workflow-level measurements: rather than ranking models, we quantify the guarded-stage marginal detection effect in a narrowly scoped, preregistered regime and place that measurement in the context of validator coverage and task curation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. We froze a machine-readable preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) before execution. Design: paired-binary (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Planned confirmatory Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). The preregistration specified a minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 (20 percentage points) for power planning targeting ≈80% power under conservative baseline assumptions.

Task bank and inclusion. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks from intent_configuration_repair_v1. The bank abstracts three vendor-CLI families (labeled vendor A/B/C) and small topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance; parser failures triggered a deterministic reseed policy (up to two automatic reseeds). For the confirmatory run no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred and complete_pair_count = 720 (see analysis/missingness_summary.csv archived artifact).

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider entry recorded as openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null. We explicitly state that temperature = null denotes no explicit temperature parameter was supplied in the request; it does not imply deterministic sampling or temperature=0. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics a single sampled initial candidate per task was recorded and reused by both baseline and guarded condition scorers; consequently any between-condition discordance can arise only from (i) guarded-stage emulation observations that reveal a violation not encoded as a static validator rule or (ii) the permitted downstream repair-stage invocation (one repair permitted per task).

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline implementation. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 executing full intent-constraint validation (syntax, workflow ordering, required-field presence, and policy-level constraints). Guarded: baseline validator followed by a sandboxed emulation harness that applies the candidate configuration against the emulated topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. The repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model call per task; run accounting shows exactly one repair-stage call in the confirmatory execution. All per-episode validator and emulation traces, candidate texts, and scorer outputs were recorded and archived.

Scoring, missingness handling, and analysis executor. Outcome per pair is binary: detected_by_baseline ∈ {0,1} and detected_by_guarded ∈ {0,1}. Missingness: parser or infrastructure failures handled deterministically (automatic reseed up to two times; irrecoverable failures replaced per missingness_plan). Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor with complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs). We report both the exact McNemar two-sided test (as executed by the analysis executor) and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI using 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Secondary per-class/vendor comparisons were preregistered as exploratory with Bonferroni-adjusted intervals.
sections.results:
Confirmatory primary outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). The archived paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) contains: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline_success_rate = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded_success_rate = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These values are produced by the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and are available as analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Authoritative execution accounting (execution/execution_manifest.json summarized in the archive) reports model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared_initial_generation + 1 repair-stage call) and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the unique mechanisms for the single n10 discordance are (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not covered by the static validator, or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. For independent verification the discordant episode can be located by scanning the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl for the unique record with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that record contains the pair_id and the per-episode validator and emulation traces. (File: execution/raw_results.jsonl; archived SHA-256: df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8. See also analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, SHA-256: 49731a2e52e049ccf5b53c35ddac2351ad75e7e95504dc4a42bcb096d0dec3aa, which corroborates stage accounting and the single repair-stage call.)

Representative episode diagnostics. The archive includes representative per-episode traces (artifact_examples covering task-000001 through task-000006) showing validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, validator_version = 5.0, normalized candidates, and validation_before/validation_after states. Those examples demonstrate that most recorded candidates matched the validator rules (violation_count = 0 for the vast majority) and that emulation observations duplicated validator findings in this curated corpus. The single discordant episode is the exception and is directly discoverable in execution/raw_results.jsonl as described above.

Missingness, exclusions, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy was followed: complete_pair_count = 720 and failed_episode_count = 0; the archived analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports no exclusions or contamination flags. No deviations affecting the primary estimand are recorded in the archived deviation log; all analysis artifacts list no registered deviations.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregated benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanatory factors. First, a validator ceiling effect: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations encoded in the synthetic task bank (baseline success rate = 0.9986). Second, task curation and inclusion rules: confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items designed to exercise workflow policies but not adversarially crafted to evade the validator; this construction concentrates items inside the validator's coverage envelope. Third, shared_initial_candidate semantics and run accounting: identical initial candidates across conditions constrain discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or the single permitted repair call; provider-call audit shows exactly one repair invocation, consistent with the single n10 discordant count.

Operational interpretation and boundary conditions. The finding implies that when a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs conform to that validator's expected patterns, sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at the aggregate level. This conditional interpretation must not be generalized: in operational regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarially crafted inputs, distribution shift, stateful multi-step interactions, or validator gaps across vendor implementations, guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation can provide substantive added value. The archived per-episode traces show instances where validator and emulation agree and indicate the need for adversarial and cross-vendor stress tests to identify regimes with material guarded-stage benefit.

Statistical and design sensitivity. The study was preregistered and powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20. The realized discordant counts (n10 = 1) produce an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the design's minimum effect-of-interest. Thus the result is a narrow, well-powered near-zero finding for the specific experimental regime (synthetic tasks, deterministic validator, shared_initial_candidate semantics) rather than evidence that guarded stages are always unnecessary.

Reproducibility and artifact-driven follow-up. All code, per-episode raw results, validator and emulation traces, analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the execution bundle referenced by the preregistration. Independent verification steps: (1) open execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 df367ecc40a6...) and search for the single record with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1 to obtain pair_id and full per-episode traces; (2) confirm provider-call accounting and the single repair-stage invocation via analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 49731a...); (3) reproduce the paired analysis from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv (archived). These artifacts enable audit and targeted follow-up experiments (adversarial tasks, multi-validator comparisons).

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate guarded-stage contributions but remove generation variability between conditions; provider-side nondeterminism remains a residual uncertainty despite reconciliation checks. Construct validity: our binary detection scoring reflects intent-constraint checks and emulation-observed violations but does not quantify operational impact (downtime, rollback cost). External validity: single declared model family (gpt-5-mini), single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic, parser-validated tasks limit generalizability to adversarial or production distributions. Conclusion validity: the preregistered power plan targeted 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) is far smaller and secondary per-class/vendor estimates are exploratory. These limitations appear explicitly in the archived limitations list and are summarized below.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; archived per-episode traces permit independent verification (execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design. We recommend targeted follow-ups: adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, multiple validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the execution manifest and provider_call_audit artifacts.
